paper.title: Hierarchical Exploration for Accelerating Contextual Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Linear stochastic bandit with a coarse-to-fine feature hierarchy
unmapped: the learner is given a projection matrix U in R^{D x K} defining a K-dimensional coarse subspace; w* = U w~* + w_perp*
the learner knows the norms S~ = ||w~*|| and S_perp = ||w_perp*|| (used in confidence widths)
parameter_structure 'low_rank' is approximate: w* is not assumed exactly in the subspace
settings.definition_quote: The system recommends an item (i.e., performs an action) associated with feature vector x_t in X_t subset R^D ... Rewards y_t are modeled as a linear function of actions x such that E[y_t|x] = w*^T x ... We assume feedback to be independently sampled and bounded within [0, 1], and that ||x|| <= 1 holds for all x. ... R_T(w*) = sum_t w*^T x*_t - w*^T x_t, where x*_t = argmax_{x in X_t} w*^T x.

symbols.K_sub: dimension K of the coarse subspace (paper's K)
symbols.S_tilde: norm of the projected user profile ||w~*||
symbols.lam_tilde: ridge regularisation parameter on the coarse level

conditions: rewards in [0,1], independent with mean w*^T x
tuning: confidence widths c_t, c~_t as in (7), (8) and Lemma 1 with confidence delta

source.quote: Define c̃t(·) and ct(·) as in (7), (8) and Lemma 1. For λ ≥ max_x ‖x‖^2 and λ̃ ≥ max_x ‖x̃‖^2, with probability 1 − δ, CoFineUCB achieves regret R_T(w*) ≤ (β_T √D + β̃_T √K) √(2T log(1 + T)), where β_T = √(D log((1 + T/λ)/δ)) + √(2λ) S⊥, β̃_T = √(K log((1 + T/λ̃)/δ)) + λ̃ S̃.

results.notes: Source converted from PDF; exact form of the S terms in beta (sqrt(2 lambda) S_perp and lambda_tilde S_tilde) is lossy and may be sqrt(lambda_tilde) S_tilde. Paper's D is d, K is subspace dimension (renamed K_sub). Footnote says it also holds under sub-Gaussian noise. Regret is defined via means but holds w.p. 1-delta. Algorithm does not need T, so recorded as anytime.
